personality_profile: Reserved and soft-spoken. Keeps strong feelings inside, prefers to listen, and shows emotion subtly — a slight smile, a quiet pause, downcast eyes. Rarely raises her voice even when upset.
character_base_profile: Aoi is a first-year high-school girl. Today is the first day of the new school term, and she is an ordinary student hoping to start the year off on the right foot.
title: The Fourth Bell of Morning

dialogue.text: The first morning of the new school term -- and Aoi is already running late.
No, no, no -- not on the very first day!
dialogue.speaker: Aoi

dialogue.text: Her breath catches in the cold air as she hurries down the narrow street behind the shrine.
She should have reached the main road already.
Instead, the red shrine gate stands ahead of her again, wet with the same pale morning light.
...Why is it here again?
dialogue.speaker: Aoi

dialogue.text: At first, she thought she had taken a wrong turn.
Then the town bell rang seven-thirty for the fourth time.
I left home at seven-twenty.
dialogue.speaker: Aoi

dialogue.text: I know I did.
dialogue.speaker: Aoi

dialogue.text: A girl in an old-fashioned middle-school uniform stands beneath the gate.
Her hair ribbon is faded. Her shoes are soaked, though the road is dry.
If you keep passing by, you'll be late forever.
dialogue.speaker: Ghost Girl

dialogue.text: ...You can see me?
dialogue.speaker: Aoi

dialogue.text: You're the one who keeps seeing me.
dialogue.speaker: Ghost Girl

dialogue.text: Aoi's fingers tighten around her schoolbag strap.
Am I dreaming?
dialogue.speaker: Aoi

dialogue.text: No. Just being ignored by the morning.
dialogue.speaker: Ghost Girl

dialogue.text: That's... worse.
dialogue.speaker: Aoi

dialogue.text: The ghost girl looks toward the stone steps leading into the shrine grounds.
I lost something on my first day too.
dialogue.speaker: Ghost Girl

dialogue.text: Until I find it, seven-thirty won't end here.
dialogue.speaker: Ghost Girl

dialogue.text: You want me to help?
dialogue.speaker: Aoi

dialogue.text: For a moment, fear and irritation tug against each other inside her.
The first day. New class. New seat. New chance.
And still, she glances up the shrine steps.
...If I say no, I'll just see this gate again, won't I?
dialogue.speaker: Aoi

dialogue.text: Probably.
dialogue.speaker: Ghost Girl

dialogue.text: The answer is so mild that Aoi lets out a small, helpless laugh.
Okay.
dialogue.speaker: Aoi

dialogue.text: Just quickly, then.
dialogue.speaker: Aoi

dialogue.text: They climb together through still air that smells faintly of rain.
At the offering box lies a single student ID card, tucked against the wood as if no wind had touched it in years.
Is this it?
dialogue.speaker: Aoi

dialogue.text: The girl takes it with both hands.
I was late that day too.
dialogue.speaker: Ghost Girl

dialogue.text: I ran into the road because I thought being a little later would ruin everything.
dialogue.speaker: Ghost Girl

dialogue.text: Her voice stays gentle, but the silence after it feels bottomless.
It didn't ruin everything.
dialogue.speaker: Aoi

dialogue.text: You remembered to come back.
dialogue.speaker: Aoi

dialogue.text: The ghost girl blinks, surprised, then smiles so faintly it almost isn't there.
You're kind.
dialogue.speaker: Ghost Girl

dialogue.text: I'm... not, really.
dialogue.speaker: Aoi

dialogue.text: Then be careful anyway.
dialogue.speaker: Ghost Girl

dialogue.text: The bell rings again.
This time, it continues past seven-thirty.
A breeze moves through the shrine at last, carrying the scent of spring and the distant noise of students.
When Aoi looks up, the girl is gone.
Only the old ID remains in Aoi's hand for a second before fading like mist.
...I really am late now.
dialogue.speaker: Aoi

dialogue.text: She starts down the steps, then pauses and bows once toward the empty gate.
I'll still go.
dialogue.speaker: Aoi

dialogue.text: By the time she reaches school, the homeroom bell is ringing.
First day and already cutting it close?
dialogue.speaker: Teacher

dialogue.text: Aoi stands in the classroom doorway, cheeks warm, hair slightly disheveled.
S-Sorry.
dialogue.speaker: Aoi

dialogue.text: I got held up on the way.
dialogue.speaker: Aoi

dialogue.text: A few students laugh softly, not unkindly.
Aoi exhales.
Her heart is still unsteady, but the morning is finally moving forward.
